facts.statement: A Kansas non-commercial Class C instructional permit requires the applicant to be at least 14.
Kansas lists 17 as the minimum age for an unrestricted non-commercial Class C license.
An internet driver-education completion certificate is not accepted for Kansas licensing.
Kansas-approved school-district driver education must come from an accredited district with Department of Education approval.
An approved private driver-education program provides 8 classroom hours.
An approved private driver-education program includes 6 hours of behind-the-wheel instruction.
The department recommends arranging an appointment before visiting a licensing office.
Eligible Kansas applicants may complete the non-commercial knowledge exam online and bring the passing result to avoid the office knowledge exam.
Driving a motor vehicle on Kansas public roads requires a driver license.
A new Kansas resident must obtain a Kansas driver license within 90 days of moving into the state.
An applicant must provide proof of name, age and address.
Applicants below 18 need parental or guardian consent.
Applicants must surrender driver licenses or identification cards they previously held.
An applicant with suspended, revoked, denied or cancelled driving privileges is disqualified under the handbook's eligibility list.
Kansas licensing requires lawful presence in the United States.
Applicants must meet the medical conditions for their requested license type.
Unpaid moving-violation fines prevent meeting the listed licensing requirements.
The passenger-car handbook does not replace the separate commercial-vehicle manual for commercial licensing.
Motorcycle licensing requires study of the separate motorcycle manual in addition to this handbook.
A farm-permit applicant must be at least 14 and younger than 17.
A farm-permit applicant must live on a farm or have paid employment on one.
For the farm-permit rule, a farm has at least 20 acres devoted to agricultural use.
A farm employer must sign an affidavit confirming the applicant's farm employment.
The farm-permit process requires an affidavit signed by a parent or guardian and the employer.
A farm-permit applicant must pass vision, written and driving exams or present the DE-99 driver-education completion slip.
A farm-permit driver aged 14 or 15 may drive for farm work, employment or other farm-related work.
A farm-permit driver aged 14 or 15 may use the most direct home-school route to attend school, excluding school activities.
Farm-permit drivers aged 14 or 15 may not carry minor passengers who are not siblings.
A farm-permit driver may use a wireless device only to report unlawful activity or request emergency help.
Before receiving the lesser farm-permit restrictions for ages 16 and 17, an applicant needs a parental or guardian affidavit confirming at least 50 practice hours.
The farm-permit practice affidavit for lesser restrictions must include at least 10 nighttime hours.
Farm-permit holders under the lesser restrictions may drive between 5 a.m. and 9 p.m.
A lesser-restricted farm-permit driver may travel to or from school and authorized school activities.
A lesser-restricted farm-permit driver may travel to or from an activity held by a religious organization.
Lesser-restricted farm-permit driving is permitted for work, employment and farm-related duties.
A lesser-restricted farm-permit driver may drive while a licensed adult occupies the front passenger seat.
The lesser-restricted farm-permit path allows only one minor passenger from outside the driver's immediate family.
A farm-permit applicant below 17 must have held a state learner permit for at least one year before license issuance.
At age 16, holding a lesser-restricted license or farm permit for 6 months removes the listed age restrictions.
An instructional-permit applicant younger than 16 needs a parent's or guardian's written application.
A parent or guardian signs the instructional-permit affidavit at the licensing office when applying.
For a Class C instructional permit, pass the vision and written exams or bring the DE99 form authorizing the permit from the approved driver-education course you are attending.
A Class C instructional permit expires after one year and may be renewed with testing.
An instructional-permit holder may drive only with a licensed adult seated in front.
The adult supervising an instructional-permit driver must be at least 21.
The adult supervising an instructional-permit driver needs at least one year of driving experience.
The supervising adult is the only person permitted in the front seat beside an instructional-permit driver.
An instructional-permit driver may use a wireless device only for reporting illegal activity or obtaining emergency assistance.
A restricted-license applicant must be at least 15.
A restricted-license applicant must have held a state learner permit for at least one year, excluding time on a driver-education permit slip.
A restricted-license applicant aged 15 needs 25 supervised practice hours.
Restricted-license applicants aged 15 must complete approved driver education, while applicants aged 16 do not have that requirement.
Restricted-license applicants aged 16 need 50 supervised practice hours.
Of the practice required for restricted-license applicants aged 16, 10 hours must be at night.
A parent or guardian must attest by affidavit to the restricted-license applicant's supervised practice.
A restricted-license driver aged 15 with only 25 supervised hours must submit another affidavit for 25 additional hours, including 10 at night, before moving to the restrictions for ages 16 and 17.
For the restricted Class C practice requirement at age 15, the accompanying adult must be at least 21.
For the less-restricted Class C practice requirement at age 16, the accompanying adult must be at least 21.
For less-restricted farm-permit practice at age 16, the accompanying adult must be at least 21.
A restricted-license applicant aged 16 must pass the vision, written and driving exams or present the DE-99 driver-education completion slip.
An applicant below 18 must complete approved driver education when that requirement applies to the applicant's Kansas licensing path.
The handbook includes a court finding of mental incompetence among the conditions that prevent meeting its licensing eligibility list.

changed_existing_facts.original_statement: An approved private driver-education program provides 6 hours of driving instruction.
changed_existing_facts.corrected_statement: An approved private driver-education program includes 6 hours of behind-the-wheel instruction.
changed_existing_facts.issue: The six-hour component specifically requires behind-the-wheel instruction; generic driving instruction does not preserve its format.

changed_existing_facts.original_statement: An applicant must provide proof of identity, age and address.
changed_existing_facts.corrected_statement: An applicant must provide proof of name, age and address.
changed_existing_facts.issue: Identity replaces the source's narrower proof-of-name wording.

changed_existing_facts.original_statement: A suspended, revoked, denied or cancelled license can disqualify an applicant from driving privileges.
changed_existing_facts.corrected_statement: An applicant with suspended, revoked, denied or cancelled driving privileges is disqualified under the handbook's eligibility list.
changed_existing_facts.issue: Can disqualify weakens a stated disqualification into a possibility.

changed_existing_facts.original_statement: Farm-permit applicants must pass vision, written and driving exams unless they present the driver-education completion slip.
changed_existing_facts.corrected_statement: A farm-permit applicant must pass vision, written and driving exams or present the DE-99 driver-education completion slip.
changed_existing_facts.issue: The form is unnamed in the standalone statement; the source specifies DE-99.

changed_existing_facts.original_statement: Lesser-restricted farm-permit driving is permitted for school attendance and authorized school activities.
changed_existing_facts.corrected_statement: A lesser-restricted farm-permit driver may travel to or from school and authorized school activities.
changed_existing_facts.issue: For school could allow driving beyond travel to and from school or an authorized activity.

changed_existing_facts.original_statement: Lesser-restricted farm-permit driving is permitted for activities held by a religious organization.
changed_existing_facts.corrected_statement: A lesser-restricted farm-permit driver may travel to or from an activity held by a religious organization.
changed_existing_facts.issue: The source authorizes travel to and from the activity, rather than unrestricted driving for it.

changed_existing_facts.original_statement: Instructional-permit applicants need vision and written exams or the qualifying form from their current approved driver-education course.
changed_existing_facts.corrected_statement: For a Class C instructional permit, pass the vision and written exams or bring the DE99 form authorizing the permit from the approved driver-education course you are attending.
changed_existing_facts.issue: Qualifying form is not self-contained and omits the source's DE99 form identifier and permit authorization.

changed_existing_facts.original_statement: An instructional permit lasts one year and can be renewed with testing.
changed_existing_facts.corrected_statement: A Class C instructional permit expires after one year and may be renewed with testing.
changed_existing_facts.issue: An instructional permit broadens a class-specific one-year duration; other non-commercial permit classes differ in the same section.

changed_existing_facts.original_statement: A driver licensed at 15 with only 25 practice hours needs a further affidavit for another 25 hours, including 10 at night, before moving to the older group's restrictions.
changed_existing_facts.corrected_statement: A restricted-license driver aged 15 with only 25 supervised hours must submit another affidavit for 25 additional hours, including 10 at night, before moving to the restrictions for ages 16 and 17.
changed_existing_facts.issue: Older group is not self-contained; the source specifies the age-sixteen-to-seventeen restrictions.

debts.text: The source eligibility list includes a substance or alcohol abuse problem and habitual illegal-drug use, but the grammatical reach of its court-finding condition is unclear. Preserve both conditions as unresolved source debt before teaching a resolved eligibility rule.
